question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Make head or tail of something

options.text: To earn enough for one’s needs
To make the best of an opportunity

solution:
The correct answer is- 'To figure out something.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The meaning of the given idiom is:
 
 
• To make head or tail of something means *to understand someone or something*. (किसी को या किसी चीज को समझने की कोशिश करना।)

 
 
• Example: *After spending hours working with the new piece of software, I still could not **make heads or tails **out of it*.
 
 
 
 
 
• "**To figure out**" means to understand someone or something, or to find the answer to something by thinking. (किसी को या किसी चीज़ को समझना, या सोच समझ कर किसी बात का उत्तर खोजना)
 
• By the above meaning and example, we can say that 'To figure out something' is the correct answer.
 
 
• Example - I'm trying** to figure out **a way to make this work.
 
 

Hence *option 2 *is the appropriate answer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's learn more about the given idiom:
 
 
• This idiom is **not **used in its *original form *instead it is used in the **negative form**. It means it is used when you want to express that you are **unable to understand **anything about *something *or *someone*.

 
 
• **Example:** *We couldn’t **make heads or tails **of your directions.*
